prompt: Does the LGPD apply to a nine-person bookshop with a customer list?

choices.text: No, because it does not sell to other countries
choices.why: Processing in Brazil is enough.

choices.text: Only if it holds sensitive data
choices.why: Any personal data is covered.

choices.text: Yes, in a simplified form
choices.why: Right. Resolution CD/ANPD no. 2 of 2022.

choices.text: No, only to companies with more than 250 staff
choices.why: There is no such threshold in the law.

prompt: Match each item to its category under the LGPD.

pairs.left: 1,200 orders shipped to São Paulo in September

prompt: The shop removes customers' names from an export but keeps street address, date of birth and order history. Is that anonymised data?

choices.text: Yes, since no name remains
choices.why: Identifiable is enough to be personal data.

choices.text: Only the date of birth is personal data
choices.why: All of it relates to identifiable people.

choices.text: Yes, if the file is encrypted
choices.why: Encryption protects data; it does not anonymise it.

choices.text: No: they remain identifiable
choices.why: Right. Still personal data, still under the law.

prompt: How many legal bases does article 7 of the LGPD list?
Match each of the shop's processing activities to its legal basis.

pairs.left: checking an order is not fraud

prompt: Why does the lesson say consent should not be the default basis?
hint: What happens when the person says no?

choices.text: A withdrawal stops the process
choices.why: Right. Another basis that fits is more stable.

choices.text: Consent forms are too expensive
choices.why: Cost is not the argument.

choices.text: Consent is illegal in Brazil
choices.why: It is basis I of article 7.

choices.text: The ANPD must approve every consent
choices.why: No such approval exists.

prompt: Under legitimate interest, which use passes and which does not, in the lesson's example?
hint: Weigh it against the person's expectations.

choices.text: Both pass, since legitimate interest covers any business purpose
choices.why: It is not a blank cheque.

choices.text: Selling passes if the price is fair
choices.why: Price does not change the balance.

choices.text: Fraud checks pass; selling history does not
choices.why: Right. A light intrusion against an unexpected one.

choices.text: Neither passes; only consent covers them
choices.why: Fraud prevention fits legitimate interest.

prompt: Which LGPD principle says to collect only the minimum data needed?
hint: No ID document to sell a book.

choices.text: Free access
choices.why: Free access is about people finding out what is done.

choices.text: Data quality
choices.why: Quality is about accuracy.

choices.text: Necessity
choices.why: Right. The cheapest security control there is.

choices.text: Transparency
choices.why: Transparency is about clear information.

prompt: A message from an unknown address asks for "all the data you hold about me", signed with a customer's name. What must the shop do first?

choices.text: Forward it to the ANPD
choices.why: The ANPD does not handle each request.

choices.text: Send the data, since access is a right
choices.why: Sending them to a stranger is a leak.

choices.text: Verify the request comes from that customer
choices.why: Right. Otherwise the right of access becomes a way to steal data.

choices.text: Refuse, since requests by email are invalid
choices.why: Email requests are fine once the person is verified.

prompt: Match each customer request to the right it exercises.

pairs.left: "my address is wrong, please fix it"
"stop the newsletter and delete me from it"
pairs.right: deletion of data processed with consent

pairs.left: "who have you shared my data with?"

right_distractors: right to be forgotten by the internet

prompt: Which three of the ten principles does the lesson call this course under other names?

choices.text: Consent, contract and legitimate interest
choices.why: Those are legal bases, not principles.

choices.text: Security, prevention and accountability
choices.why: Right. With necessity as the cheapest control.

choices.text: Free access, quality and non-discrimination
choices.why: Those are about people's access and fairness.

choices.text: Purpose, adequacy and transparency
choices.why: Those are about telling people and keeping to it.

prompt: Under Resolution CD/ANPD no. 15 of 2024, within how many working days must a serious incident be communicated?
hint: From when the controller learns of it.

prompt: An incident involving personal data is judged not to need communication. What does the shop still do?

choices.text: Records it, with the reasoning
choices.why: Right. A decision with a reason and a name.

choices.text: Communicates it anyway, a month later
choices.why: The record is what the rule asks for.

choices.text: Deletes the logs so no evidence remains
choices.why: That would destroy the evidence the record needs.

choices.text: Nothing, since it was not communicated
choices.why: Every incident is recorded.

prompt: How does article 46 relate to lesson 1?

choices.text: It applies only to availability
choices.why: It covers all three.

choices.text: It lists the 93 Annex A controls by name
choices.why: It lists no controls.

choices.text: It requires ISO 27001 certification
choices.why: No certification is required.

choices.text: It states the CIA triad in legal language
choices.why: Right. And leaves the how to the organisation.

prompt: What is the maximum simple fine under article 52 for one infraction?

choices.text: 10% of worldwide revenue, with no cap
choices.why: That is not the LGPD's rule.

choices.text: 1% of profit, limited to R$ 1 million
choices.why: Neither the base nor the cap is right.

choices.text: 2% of revenue in Brazil, limited to R$ 50 million
choices.why: Right. Per infraction.

choices.text: R$ 50 thousand, fixed
choices.why: The cap is fifty million, and it is a ceiling.

prompt: The company hosting the shop's website stores customer data following the shop's instructions. What is it under the LGPD?

choices.text: The encarregado
choices.why: That is a person, the channel to data subjects and the ANPD.

choices.text: A data subject
choices.why: Data subjects are the people the data is about.

choices.text: An operator
choices.why: Right. It processes on the controller's behalf.

choices.text: The controller
choices.why: The shop decides; the shop is the controller.

prompt: Why should the contract with an operator require it to report incidents to the shop quickly?

choices.text: The shop's three working days start when it learns
choices.why: Right. A late report from the operator eats the shop's deadline.

choices.text: Because the contract replaces the controller's duties
choices.why: Being the controller cannot be contracted away.

choices.text: So the operator can communicate to the ANPD instead
choices.why: The controller communicates.

choices.text: Because operators are the ones fined
choices.why: Both can answer; that is not the reason.

prompt: Under the simplified regime for small agents, what remains fully in force?

choices.text: Only the deadlines, which become shorter
choices.why: Some deadlines become longer.

choices.text: The obligation to name an encarregado
choices.why: Small agents may provide a channel instead.

choices.text: The security and reporting duties
choices.why: Right. Those duties stay.

choices.text: Nothing; small agents are exempt
choices.why: They are simplified, not exempt.

prompt: Which of these does the shop need to meet a three-working-day deadline? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: logs that show what an incident touched
choices.why: Lessons 10 and 11.

choices.text: an inventory of what personal data it holds and where
choices.why: Lesson 16.

choices.text: a decision in advance on who decides and writes
choices.why: Lesson 10's tabletop.

choices.text: an ISO 27001 certificate
choices.why: Not required by the LGPD.
